title: First server over stdio with the Python SDK

concept.heading: A decorator turns a typed function into a tool a host can call
paragraphs: The SDK's MCPServer keeps a registry much like yours. @server.tool() on a function reads its name, its docstring and its type hints, builds the JSON Schema, and registers it. When a host sends tools/call, the SDK validates the arguments, calls your function, and wraps whatever it returns as the result. You write three functions; the protocol is handled.

Keep the Module 1 registry underneath. Each MCP tool function calls registry.call(name, arguments) and returns the dict, so validation and errors-as-data still happen in one place, and the error dict rides inside a normal result with isError false, where the model can read it. Do not let a missing donor become a JSON-RPC error: hosts show those to the user as failures.

stdio means the host launches your server as a subprocess and talks over stdin and stdout. That is how Claude Desktop and Claude Code run local servers, and it is how the check runs yours: it spawns python -m mcp_server.server, lists the tools, and calls find_donor.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: Publishing a custom connector's actions. The decorator is the action definition; the docstring is the summary the orchestrator reads; the type hints are the request schema you filled in by hand before.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: decorators and keyword-only arguments
pythonBlock.intro: A decorator is a function that takes a function and returns one. @server.tool() registers the function as a side effect and returns it unchanged.

spec: Run uv sync --extra mcp once. Implement build_server: an MCPServer named lakeshore-donor-ops, version 0.1.0, with INSTRUCTIONS, and three @server.tool() functions whose names, parameters and docstrings match the Module 1 contracts.
Each tool calls the Module 1 registry and returns its dict, including {error: ...} results; a missing donor must not become a protocol error.
Run the server by hand and watch it wait on stdin, then open MCP Inspector against it: npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector uv run --directory middleware python -m mcp_server.server.
Call find_donor from Inspector with 'alvarez' and read the raw JSON-RPC on the wire.
askClaudeFor: A scaffold of build_server with the three decorated functions and empty bodies.
How the SDK derives inputSchema from type hints, so you can confirm Literal and Optional render as in Module 1.
writeYourself: The three tool bodies and the docstrings (copy your Module 1 descriptions on purpose: same contract, new transport).
The since conversion: an MCP date arrives as a string; the registry wants the same.
